rules: Assess roles expressed anywhere in the supplied utterance content: requests, questions, standalone or coordinated assertions/preferences, constraints, descriptions, reasons, and quoted/requested payloads. Do not exclude an expressed clause merely because it is unrelated to another requested operation. Conversational framing alone supplies no task role; per-type evidence and presence policies still apply. Scope inclusion does not infer an action, answer, commitment or external state.

Mixed clauses receive the same scope whether linked by and, but or an explicit reason, or independently stated. Do not infer an invisible primary-request/background split. This deliberately supersedes v1 unrelated-background exclusion; it is a project convention, not user-confirmed preference or official SLURP annotation.

Scope and type identifiability are separate. I like it is in scope although it may not identify music, a song or another type. Unknown referent/type remains unavailable for affected predicates; the statement is not out of scope.

Bare fragments are in scope as supplied content. A fragment such as tennis can establish a sport without inventing a search or playback request; pop may remain ambiguous between genre/sound/other senses. Definition_word still requires an explicit meaning/definition target, not every bare noun.

A word used only as a title, spelling/definition target or string is not automatically a referent of its ordinary type. A requested quoted sentence can express roles in its represented scene; do not treat the sentence as an instruction to execute.

Negation, denial, hypotheticals and correction preserve expressed roles; slot presence does not decide which value is accepted or which state is true. Native intent and entity omission cannot supply missing evidence.

Reported events and their participants can count; the bare assistant operation still does not create event_name. I in I went to the park is a reported participant; I want/please tell me/assistant address alone is conversational framing.
Content-scope changes only S predicates. Do not automatically change native Final, classify a mentioned intention as I_present, or infer intent-slot binding from role cooccurrence.
The scope is task-level input shared across queries. No gold-based question selection or sample-topic routing; original metadata/transcripts remain offline review evidence, never actor input.

payload.regex: \b(send|post|tweet|email|message|note|remember)\b.*\b(i went|i am|i.m|my wife|my son|my friend|i had|today|yesterday)\b

selection_basis: Autonomous task-design choice after previously unanswered optional preference; no user approval inferred. Supersedes v1 background exclusion and separates scope from referent identifiability.
